A_target.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be the [[Definition:Simplex|simplex]] with [[Definition:Vertex of Simplex|vertices]] $e_1, \ldots, e_n$.
Let $C_1, \ldots, C_n$ be [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed sets]] such that for all $S \subseteq \set {1, \ldots, n}$:
:$\map {\operatorname {conv} } {\set {e_i: i \in S} } \subseteq \displaystyle \bigcup_{i \mathop \in S} C_i$
Then:
:$\displaystyle \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n C_i \ne \O$

B_source.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Triangulation|triangulation]] of $\Delta$ with a proper [[Definition:Sperner Labelling|Sperner labelling]].
Then $T$ contains a cell whose vertices carry all $n$ labels.

substitutions.the vertex labels: the index of a closed set containing that vertex
substitutions.the rainbow cell: a small simplex meeting every C_i
substitutions.the fixed triangulation: a sequence of triangulations with mesh tending to zero

derived.the limit of rainbow cells: a point lying in every C_i

validity_conditions: the sets C_i must be closed for the intersection of limits to remain inside them
the covering condition on faces is exactly what makes the induced labelling proper
compactness of the simplex is needed to extract a convergent subsequence
proof_plan: Let $T_k$ be a [[Definition:Triangulation|triangulation]] of $\Delta$ of [[Definition:Mesh of Triangulation|mesh]] at most $\dfrac 1 k$.
For a vertex $v$ in the face spanned by $\set {e_i: i \in S}$, choose a label $i \in S$ with $v \in C_i$.

By the covering hypothesis such an $i$ exists.
As the label is chosen from the support of $v$, the labelling is proper in the sense of [[Sperner's Lemma]].
By [[Sperner's Lemma]], there is a cell $\sigma_k$ carrying all $n$ labels, so $\sigma_k$ meets every $C_i$.
